'''Saly Ruth Ramler''' (1894–1993), also known as Saly Ruth Struik, was the first woman to receive a [[PhD]] in [[mathematics]] from the German University in [[Prague]], now known as [[Charles University]].<ref name="intelligencer">{{cite journal |last1=Bečvářová |first1=Martina |title=Saly Ruth Struik, 1894–1993 |journal=The Mathematical Intelligencer |date=2018 |volume=40 |issue=4 |pages=79–85|doi=10.1007/s00283-018-9835-1 |s2cid=126187647 }}</ref>  

== Life and work ==
Her 1919 dissertation, on the axioms of [[affine geometry]], was supervised by [[Gerhard Kowalewski]] and [[Georg Alexander Pick]].<ref name="mathgenealogy">{{cite web |title=Saly Ruth (Ramler) Struik |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=62506 |website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project |accessdate=5 November 2018}}</ref> She married the Dutch mathematician and historian of mathematics [[Dirk Jan Struik]] in 1923. Between 1924 and 1926, the pair traveled through Europe and met many prominent mathematicians, using Dirk Struik's Rockefeller fellowship. In 1926, they emigrated to the United States, and Dirk Struik accepted a position at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Remembering Dirk Jan Struik, 1894-2000 |url=https://www.maa.org/news/remembering-dirk-jan-struik-1894-2000 |website=Mathematical Association of America |accessdate=6 November 2018 |archive-date=15 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200815114020/https://www.maa.org/news/remembering-dirk-jan-struik-1894-2000 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
